subject: Ops runbook draft: traffic segmentation + control/data handshake for private deploy
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Greg Turner <greg.turner@acmecloud.com>, infra@acmecloud.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Ops runbook draft: traffic segmentation + control/data handshake for private deploy

Hi Greg + infra team,

Attached is our initial ops runbook draft for the private deployment we discussed on Fri. The goal here is to capture the recommended traffic segmentation, how the control-plane and data-plane handshake will be established across the peering, and the fallback behavior if the control-plane path is degraded. High-level items included:

- Split-horizon DNS for control vs data endpoints
- mTLS between control-plane agents and control API (mutual cert rotation cadence)
- Egress-proxy pattern for telemetry and SAML metadata refreshes
- Traffic shaping for model-weights downloads (off-peak prefetch)
- Runbook steps for fail-open vs fail-close decisions

Please review section 3 ("Handshake sequence") and the diagram I linked in the doc. I called out two open questions where we need your input:
1) Whether Acme prefers a reverse-proxy in your VPC or direct service-to-service TLS (we prefer reverse-proxy for auditability).
2) Certificate storage expectations (KMS vs HSM).

Attachments: ops-runbook-draft.md (runbook & diagram links inline).

Can you provide feedback by EOD Wednesday so we can freeze the runbook for the pilot?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | irene@redwood.ai

From: Greg Turner <greg.turner@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@acmecloud.com, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ops runbook draft: traffic segmentation + control/data handshake for private deploy

Irene,

Thanks for the thorough draft — good coverage. A few inline notes and the Acme diagram are attached (acme-handshake-diagram.pdf). Quick answers to your two questions:

1) Reverse-proxy: Acme Infra prefers a reverse-proxy in the customer VPC for TLS termination and centralized logging. We can place a lightweight NGINX/Envoy pair in the peered subnet.
2) Cert storage: we use HSM-backed storage for private keys; KMS is acceptable for short-lived service certs but not for long-term keys.

Other comments:
- We suggest a short-lived (8 hour) control-plane token for agent registration, refreshed via the HSM-backed signing service.
- For model weights prefetch, we want explicit bandwidth caps on the data plane to avoid noisy neighbor effects; adding a dedicated egress queue for model transfers should be fine.

Attaching acme-handshake-diagram.pdf and a small text file with our certificate policy (mtls-cert-proposal.txt).

I'll loop in Rachel Lee from the pilot customer to confirm their network constraints.

—Greg
Greg Turner
Platform Engineering, Acme Cloud
greg.turner@acmecloud.com

Attachments: acme-handshake-diagram.pdf (diagram), mtls-cert-proposal.txt

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Greg Turner <greg.turner@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ops runbook draft: traffic segmentation + control/data handshake for private deploy

Folks,

Thanks Greg — the reverse-proxy approach aligns with our telemetry requirements. A couple of technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- Control-plane traffic is low RPS but sensitive; we need GC-friendly keepalives on the proxy to avoid connection churn when agents are idle. Recommend HTTP/2 with long-lived streams for control commands.
- Data-plane (inference requests) should support direct passthrough to a local serving pool after initial auth; the proxy should not be the bottleneck for inference throughput. We can add a signed short-lived ticket that the proxy exchanges for a direct data token.
- For cert rotation: propose a staggered rotation to avoid simultaneous invalidation (pilot region rotates at 03:00 UTC, office region at 05:00 UTC).

Open action for Monica: can you draft the token exchange sequence and a sample TTL for tickets? Also, Monica — please call out operational metrics we want from the proxy (latency p95, connection counts, auth failures) so Acme can expose them.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Greg Turner <greg.turner@acmecloud.com>, infra@acmecloud.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@corpclient.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ops runbook draft: traffic segmentation + control/data handshake for private deploy

Alex / Greg / Rachel — thanks for the quick turns. Consolidating next steps below so we have a clear owner list before we freeze the runbook: 

1) Acme Infra (Greg) — confirm proxy sizing and placement (edge-subnet vs peering-subnet) and share resource estimate by Wed EOD. Deliverable: proxy-sizing.pdf (drop in shared Drive).
2) Monica Patel (Redwood) — draft token exchange sequence (example TTLs: control token 8h, data ticket 10m) and the proxy metric list. Target: Tue EOD.
3) Jonas Weber (Redwood) — add the HTTP/2 long-lived stream recommendations to section 3.2 and the staggered cert rotation schedule. Target: Tue noon.
4) Rachel Lee (Pilot customer) — confirm any outbound firewall egress restrictions and whether ACME proxy needs to use a customer NAT.

Decision items:
- We will adopt Acme's HSM for long-term private keys and use KMS for short-lived control tokens.
- Implement reverse-proxy in Acme's peering-subnet as the preferred pattern for pilot.

I've updated ops-runbook-draft.md with the action items and linked the Acme diagram from the Drive. If everyone can hit their targets, we'll freeze the runbook on Thurs and schedule the pilot cutover for the following week.

Thanks — appreciate the partnership on this.

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | irene@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: ops-runbook-draft.md (updated), acme-handshake-diagram.pdf (linked), mtls-cert-proposal.txt (attached)
